plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: hallmark GSVA sample scores
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate ulcerative-colitis inflamed colon from control. The inputs are a 12,000 x 12 raw integer gene-level count matrix from Salmon (gene symbols in the first column of counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata table carrying one condition column, 6 inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Six per group is exactly the replicate regime where a per-sample score method is well behaved, so GSVA on the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets is the central step, with limma on the score matrix using the same design as the gene-level model, and a clustered heatmap of the 50 hallmark scores annotated by condition as the deliverable figure. The profile flags sample_01 with a library size about 4x below the median: it is kept through QC and inspected on the PCA and the distance heatmap rather than dropped, because DESeq2 size factors already account for depth, and because with 6 per group dropping a sample costs real power. Depth still matters more for GSVA than for the count model — GSVA ranks genes within each sample, so a shallow library has more ties and a compressed rank distribution — hence the score step runs on VST values (Gaussian kernel) rather than raw counts, and the report must state explicitly whether sample_01 is the outlier on the score heatmap. The gene-level DESeq2 Wald test runs first because it supplies the tested-gene universe, the Wald statistic used for the confirmatory fgsea preranked pass, and the differentially expressed genes that let a hallmark score be interpreted. The hallmark GMT is present in the reference store for human (2026.1), so the central step is supported; GO BP is present as an optional follow-up collection and its absence would cost only an annotation. Note the ceiling: 12 samples, no independent cohort, so a pathway that separates the groups here is a hypothesis, not a validated discriminator, and the heatmap ordering must not be presented as a classifier.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
~ condition with control as explicit reference level
GSVA per-sample hallmark pathway scores with limma on the score matrix, plus fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic
Reproducibility and interpretation report with hallmark heatmap, MA and dispersion plots

Significant sets are mapped back to the hallmark sets from T2S1 they annotate, so each hallmark hit has supporting specific processes where they exist
Overlapping GO sets are collapsed to representative terms before any count of findings is reported
constraints: Rank the same full tested-gene list by the same DESeq2 Wald statistic used in T2S1 — do not change the metric between the two enrichment passes
Use a human collection only; the mouse and rat GMTs in the store must not be used
Apply the 15-500 gene size window after intersection with the tested genes
Collapse redundant, nested sets (GO in particular shares members between parent and child terms) before reporting a count of findings
Set and record the random seed
caveats: GO is a nested hierarchy, so blocks of correlated significant terms are expected and are one finding, not many
This step is annotation, not evidence — if the second collection is unavailable the primary hallmark result from T2S1 still stands

grounding.reason: Human dataset: a second curated collection after hallmark per R-0098@d01b and R-0048@500d, with redundant sets collapsed per R-0052@620a. Reactome is the named preference; the step falls back to the GO/WikiPathways collections actually present and must say so.

steps.name: Integrated report
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed colon from control in these 12 samples, how strong is that evidence, and what are the limits of the claim?
steps.context: Assembles T1S1, T1S2, T2S1 and T2S2 into one report answering the user's question: the per-sample hallmark score table, the annotated hallmark heatmap as the headline figure, the ranked list of hallmarks that differ between inflamed and control, and the gene-level evidence beneath them.
steps.description: Final report: hallmark score heatmap and the ranked separating pathways as the lead result, the DESeq2 gene-level result with its diagnostics beneath it, the GSVA-versus-fgsea concordance, and a full reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Leads with the hallmark score heatmap and the ranked list of hallmark sets separating inflamed from control, with adjusted p-values and effect direction

Names the method, package versions, the ~condition design with the explicit control reference level, the contrast direction, the thresholds, the number of genes tested and the number differentially expressed
Reports the hallmark collection and version, the ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic) and why it was chosen, the tested-gene universe, and the 15-500 size window
Lists leading-edge genes per significant set and marks leading edges shared between reported sets
States the sample_01 depth issue, the decision taken on it, and its position on both the PCA and the hallmark score heatmap
States that enrichment results are method-dependent and reports the GSVA/fgsea agreement and disagreement rather than one list alone
States the power and validation ceiling explicitly: 12 samples, no independent cohort, so a separating pathway is a hypothesis and the heatmap ordering is not a classifier
Carries a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seeds used, and the pinned gene set collection versions
constraints: Include the MA plot, the dispersion plot and the p-value histogram as fit diagnostics before the gene tables
Give the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and the lfcSE for each reported gene, and rank the gene tables by the shrunken value
Do not present any hallmark set as a validated discriminator of inflamed versus control — no external cohort was analysed
Do not report a GSVA score difference without its adjusted p-value from the limma test on the score matrix
caveats: The heatmap will look convincing regardless of whether the separation is robust; the adjusted p-values from limma on the score matrix, not the visual clustering, carry the evidence

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report step: shrunken and unshrunken effects with lfcSE (R-0085@c24d), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), method/version/design/threshold reporting (R-0041@059a, R-0051@01ca), leading edges (R-0105@c4a8), method-dependence caveat (R-0055@107a) and a reproducibility record (R-0086@becf). R-0042@54e1 (two-method DE overlap) is not planned: the question is pathway-level, and a second DE tool would not change the hallmark scores.
